body.statement: Within the \(q\)-state double-triangular parameterization, \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\neq0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(M_1)=\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=q^K\). If \(d_{a,k,u}=0\), then view \(a\) is rank deficient. For \(q=3\), strictly positive local tables can have pairwise distinct conditional columns and \(d_{a,k,u}=0\).
body.justification: This is an exact local algebraic frontier rather than a generic full-rank premise.
body.gap: Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) use global Kruskal inequalities, while Lee and Gu (2026) do not characterize the categorical zero boundary.
body.consumer: It separates admissible but uncertified assessment designs from full-rank designs and identifies the failing context.
body.proof_tex:
For a square \(q^K\times q^K\) matrix, full rank is equivalent to a nonzero determinant. Theorem~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} and Definition~\textnormal{def:certificate} give
\[
 \det(M_a)\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \prod_{k=1}^{K}\prod_{u\in\mathcal Q^{k-1}}
 d_{a,k,u}^{q^{K-k}}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 d_{a,k,u}\ne0\ \text{for every }k,u.
\]
The exponents \(q^{K-k}\) are positive integers. Applying this equivalence for \(a=1,2\) proves
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}\ne0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{rank}(M_1)=\operatorname{rank}(M_2)=q^K.
\]
It also proves directly that \(d_{a,k,u}=0\) forces \(\det(M_a)=0\), hence rank deficiency of view \(a\).

The distinction between column separation and determinant nonvanishing is real already for \(q=3\). Put
\[
 b=\begin{pmatrix}1/3\\1/3\\1/3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 v=\begin{pmatrix}\delta\\-\delta\\0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 B=\begin{pmatrix}b-v&b&b+v\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad 0<\delta<1/3.
\]
Every column is a strictly positive probability vector, and the three columns are pairwise distinct. Nevertheless the first plus the third column equals twice the second, so \(\det(B)=0\). Taking this \(B\) as any local conditional table gives the asserted strictly positive ternary boundary witness.
